page: Amazon Web Services c6a.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, delivering two vCPUs across one physical core with multithreading enabled. The instance includes 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a 2:1 ratio of memory to vCPUs. It does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated graphics accelerators, relying on remote network storage for persistence. Baseline network throughput is configured at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate competitive single-thread CPU performance, highlighted by a strong stress-ng single-core score of 2985.49 and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1614.0. However, multi-core throughput and overall memory subsystem bandwidth are constrained by the dual-vCPU ceiling and single physical core allocation. Multi-core Geekbench reached 2005.0, while PassMark database operations and Redis SET throughput placed in lower tiers. Memory bandwidth tests showed 30.34 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 21.10 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From an efficiency perspective, c6a.large provides dedicated x86_64 compute capacity for processing tasks that prioritize single-core clock speeds without requiring substantial memory or local disk I/O. The lack of bundled local storage necessitates decoupled EBS volumes, which represents a critical architectural consideration. This instance type is suited for microservices, lightweight web servers, routine continuous integration steps, small batch-processing utilities, and modest inference workloads using compact language models.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro System, featuring a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with two dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core. Configured with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, it maintains a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. The virtual machine omits hardware GPU acceleration and onboard local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network capacity. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-thread compute capabilities, achieving 2985.49 in stress-ng single-core tests, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth are bounded by the low core count. With modest memory and network baselines, c6a.large is technically suited for lightweight compute tasks, small-scale web serving, dedicated microservices, CI build nodes, and small-model inference tasks that demand consistent single-thread execution without large memory footprints.
